en.title: Jesus Paid It All
en.author: Elvina M. Hall
stanzas:
[D]I hear the Sav[A7]ior [D]say,
"Thy [G]strength in[D]deed is [A7]small,
[D]Child of weakness, [G]watch and [D]pray,
Find in [A7]Me thine all in [D]all."

Lord, now indeed I find
Thy pow'r and Thine alone,
Can change the leper's spots
And melt the heart of stone.

For nothing good have I
Whereby Thy grace to claim;
I'll wash my garments white
In the blood of Calv'ry's Lamb.

And when, before the throne,
I stand in Him complete,
"Jesus died my soul to save,"
My lips shall still repeat.
en.chorus:
[D]Jesus paid it [A7]all,
All to [D]Him I owe;
[G]Sin had left a [D]crimson stain,
He [A7]washed it white as [D]snow.

notes: Text is hymnary.org's representative text (Baptist Hymnal, 1991) — the four-stanza congregational form. The Cyber Hymnal (hymnary.org/hymn/CYBER/3420) prints six stanzas in a different order and ends 'I'll lay my trophies down, all down at Jesus' feet' instead of the quoted 'Jesus died my soul to save' line; the four shipped stanzas are what hymnals print. Meter is the tune page's 6.6.7.7 with refrain, which matches the lines as shipped; the text page lists 6.6.6.6 with refrain for the same text. Chords: printed keys are D-flat (tune page) and E-flat (Cyber Hymnal), with D Major itself common in hymnals — D chosen per the guitar rule. Straightforward I-IV-V7 chart. One repair to the representative text: it prints 'Where-by' (st. 3) with a mid-word hyphen — a syllable break carried over from the score's lyric setting, not prose — written 'Whereby' as both the Cyber Hymnal and Timeless Truths (URL appended; text otherwise confirmed there) print it. Timeless Truths marks 'leper's spots' as originally 'leopard's spots'; the 'leper's' reading shipped here is the common hymnal one.
